description: We are a team of software-interested students building an indie game about surviving the 8 planets.
summary: A 3D physics Roblox game where players design survival suits from real engineering materials and test them on planets across the solar system. Every planet uses real NASA data. Every material has real physical properties. The game teaches players that space exploration is an engineering problem with no single right answer. Your suit has to handle the actual temperatures, pressures, and atmospheres that NASA has measured.
details:
What It Does

Players start on Earth inside a space station workshop, where they scavenge raw materials like aluminum, steel, aerogel, wool, and oxygen. They layer these materials onto a survival suit in any order and thickness they choose, then pick a destination, choose the hot or cold side of the planet, and teleport there to attempt a 20-minute mission: reach the beacon before their suit fails.

How It Works

Every planet in the game is built from real numbers. Surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, gravity, and atmosphere composition are pulled directly from the NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheets. The game covers nine destinations: Earth, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Gas giants use gravity at the 1-bar pressure level since they have no solid surface.

The physics simulation runs continuously during gameplay, checking:

  • Heat flow through each suit layer based on thermal conductivity
  • Oxygen depletion at the NASA life-support planning rate
  • Structural crush from pressure differentials against the shell's yield strength
  • Melting point failure if ambient temperature exceeds the shell material's limit

Material properties (density, yield strength, thermal conductivity, melting point) are real handbook values for each substance. The simulation has no predetermined outcomes; it runs the actual math each frame.

Benefits and Intended Impact

CODAG.0 teaches the real constraints of space exploration through play rather than reading. A player who wraps their suit in steel learns firsthand that high thermal conductivity means they freeze or cook, even though the shell is strong. A player who skips insulation on Venus discovers that no structural material survives 735 K. These lessons come from the data, not from scripted failure states.

The intended impact is to make planetary science intuitive and accessible, especially for younger audiences on a platform they already use. By meeting players where they are (Roblox has over 70 million daily active users), CODAG.0 lowers the barrier between NASA data and genuine understanding of why space travel is hard.

Tools and Technologies

  • Roblox Studio: Game engine and platform
  • Rojo: File-system to Roblox sync, enabling version-controlled Luau development
  • Luau: Roblox's typed scripting language (all game code)
  • TypeScript + Vite: Data pipeline for exporting planet/material JSON to Roblox-compatible Luau modules
  • Node.js: Build tooling and data export scripts
  • Claude AI (Anthropic): Used for code generation, debugging.
  • Sketchfab: Planet textures sourced from Sketchfab (Creative Commons licensed models).

What Makes It Creative

  • Total player freedom. There is no tech tree, no unlock order, and no "correct" build. Players can stack up to eight layers in any combination and discover through the simulation what works and what does not.
  • Data-driven worlds. Each planet's environment (terrain color, atmosphere haze, sky tint, fog, gravity) is generated from the data rather than hand-designed, so each world feels distinct because it genuinely is.
  • Real physics as gameplay. The game never simplifies into pass/fail categories. Players watch their body temperature climb or their oxygen tick down in real time at the actual rates the math produces.

Factors We Considered

  • Accuracy. Every number traces back to a specific NSSDC fact sheet entry. Source citations are stored alongside the data in the codebase.
  • Accessibility. The game runs on any device Roblox supports, including phones. The UI adapts for mobile screens.
  • Educational honesty. Unit conversions are only of units the fact sheets already state (km to m, bar to Pa, g/mol to kg/mol). No values are interpolated.
